practices.practice: Create one MongoClient per process and reuse it (singleton client) instead of opening a new client per request.
practices.prior_belief: Create and reuse a single long-lived MongoClient (connection pool) instance read from DOCUMENTDB_URI in the environment; do not open a new client per request.

practices.practice: Keep database credentials out of source control: read connection strings from environment variables and store production secrets in a secure vault such as Azure Key Vault; never commit or log raw connection strings.
practices.prior_belief: Keep database credentials out of source control: read the connection string from an environment variable and store secrets in Azure Key Vault (or similar) rather than files; never log the raw connection string.

practices.practice: Require TLS on all connections to the cluster (tls=true) and validate server certificates in production.
practices.prior_belief: Require TLS/SSL for connections (TLS=true in connection string) and validate server certificates when connecting to the DocumentDB cluster.

practices.practice: Tune MongoClient connection-pool and timeout parameters for your environment (maxPoolSize/minPoolSize/maxIdleTimeMS/serverSelectionTimeoutMS/socketTimeoutMS) and initialize the client outside request handlers (module/global scope).
practices.prior_belief: Configure sensible MongoClient timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) to fail fast in bad network conditions and avoid stuck requests in the agent workflow.

practices.practice: Implement retry logic for transient errors and throttling (e.g., 429), using exponential backoff and honoring retry information returned by the service; enable driver-level retryable reads/writes where appropriate.
practices.prior_belief: Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient errors and throttling (HTTP 429 or MongoDB equivalent), honoring any retry-after header returned by the server.

practices.practice: Use projection to return only the fields you need (not whole documents) to reduce RU consumption and network payload.
practices.prior_belief: Use projection to return only required fields (e.g., order id, date, total) instead of whole documents to reduce RU consumption and network payloads.
practices.source_name: Request Units in Azure Cosmos DB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB projection reduce RU usage projection 'covered queries'

practices.practice: When low-latency, index-only responses are required, create covering indexes that include the fields used in both predicates and projections so the query can be served from the index alone.
practices.prior_belief: Create covering indexes that include fields used in both query predicates and projections when you need very low-latency, index-only responses for summaries (e.g., include order_total in the index).

practices.practice: Design compound indexes using the ESR rule (Equality → Sort → Range); for order-history queries create a compound index like {customer_id: 1, order_date: -1} so customer lookups with recent-order sorts are index-covered.
practices.prior_belief: Create a compound index on the fields used for the order-history queries (for example {customer_id:1, order_date:-1}) so customer lookups and recent-order sorts are index-covered.

practices.practice: In aggregation pipelines put restrictive $match stages before $group/$sort and ensure $match predicates can use an index to avoid in-memory blocking sorts.
practices.prior_belief: When building aggregation pipelines, put $match stages before $group/$sort and ensure the $match can use an index to avoid blocking in-memory sorts.

practices.practice: Validate query performance by running explain('executionStats') on important queries and aggregation pipelines and iterate on indexes until the plan shows index scans (IXSCAN) instead of collection scans (COLLSCAN).
practices.prior_belief: Validate query performance by running explain() on important queries and aggregation pipelines and adjust indexes until the explain plan shows index seeks instead of collection scans.

practices.practice: Make seeding and migration scripts idempotent (use upsert or check-and-create) so repeated runs don't duplicate data or create conflicting indexes.
practices.prior_belief: Make seeding and migration scripts idempotent (use upsert or check-and-create) so tests and repeated runs do not duplicate data or create conflicting indexes.

practices.practice: Use bulk-write / bulk-import APIs (or insertMany with ordered=false) to seed many documents efficiently to reduce round-trips and RU cost.
practices.prior_belief: Use bulk writes (bulk_write or insert_many with ordered=False) to seed many documents efficiently and to reduce round-trips and RU cost.

practices.practice: Create a unique index on stable identifiers (for example order_id) to enforce uniqueness at the database level.
Monitor RU/s consumption, throttling, latency and resource metrics and enable diagnostic logs/alerts (Log Analytics) so you can spot hotspots and costly queries.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor RU/s consumption, request charge, throttling, latency, and index usage (metrics in the portal or via monitoring APIs) to tune throughput and indexes.

practices.practice: Capture and log the request charge (x-ms-request-charge / request charge) and operation latency for key queries to spot expensive operations.
practices.prior_belief: Capture and log request charge (if available) and operation latency for each key query in tests so you can spot expensive operations introduced by the agent.

practices.practice: Lock down network access using firewall rules, Private Endpoint / VNet or IP restrictions instead of allowing open public access.
practices.prior_belief: Lock down network access with firewall rules, VNet/private endpoints, or IP restrictions so the cluster is not publicly accessible from arbitrary IPs during development or testing.

practices.practice: Use Microsoft Entra ID (identity + RBAC) for application access and consider customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption-at-rest on regulated workloads.

For vector search create an explicit vector index choosing the algorithm by scale—IVF for small sets, HNSW for medium, DiskANN for large (M30+); set dimensions, similarity metric, and tune lBuild/lSearch/maxDegree.

practices.practice: Store embeddings with explicit metadata (model name and dimensions) and keep lightweight metadata separate so vector-only ANN searches do not load heavy document payloads; use returnStoredSource / pre-filters when combining lexical and vector retrieval.
practices.prior_belief: For vector search results, store and return lightweight metadata separately from the vector field so similarity searches only load embeddings during ANN search and fetch full document fields if needed.

practices.practice: Avoid creating unnecessary indexes: keep an index budget (typically 5–15 per collection), monitor $indexStats, hide-test-drop indexes safely, and remove unused indexes after measuring usage.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid creating unnecessary indexes: each index increases write cost and RU usage—create only the indexes used by queries and remove unused ones after measuring usage.

practices.practice: Cache frequently-read static reference data (integrated cache or external cache like Azure Managed Redis) to reduce repeated DB reads and RU charge for conversational flows.
practices.prior_belief: Cache frequently-read static reference data (product catalog, status codes) in the application or agent memory to reduce repeated DB reads and RU charge for conversational flows.

practices.practice: Prefer autoscale or appropriate provisioned throughput and pick a partition key that avoids hot partitions; use per-container throughput rather than noisy shared database-level throughput where possible to prevent 429s.

practices.practice: Avoid offset/skip-based pagination for large offsets; use continuation tokens / range-based anchors (date/_id) or the driver's cursor/continuation mechanism to paginate efficiently.
